name: HardwareX hardware article template
citation: HardwareX (Elsevier). HardwareX article template, Version 2 (June 2021), Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.5078227 (record dated July 2022), read with the HardwareX Guide for Authors (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/hardwarex/publish/guide-for-authors). The template's headings are not numbered 1..n: items 1-3 cover the title, abstract and keywords, 4-8 the specifications table, 9-26 its sections 1-7 (hardware in context to validation and characterization), 27-31 the closing statements. Item 30 is the competing-interest declaration Elsevier asks of every article; the template itself does not list it.

items.topic: Title free of acronyms and abbreviations
items.question: Does the title name the hardware and what it is for, avoiding acronyms and abbreviations where it can?

items.topic: Short abstract citing the related research
items.question: Is the abstract brief and specific (the template caps it at 200 words), and does it cite any research article that used the hardware?
Are between three and six keywords given?

items.topic: Hardware name, subject area and type
items.question: Does the table name the hardware and pick one subject area and one hardware type from the journal's lists?
Does the table name the commercial product this hardware would replace, or say plainly that none exists?
Is the open source license the designs are released under stated?
Is an approximate cost of the hardware given, consistent with the bill of materials total?
Is the DOI of the source files in an approved repository (OSF, Mendeley Data, Zenodo) given, plus the OSHWA UID if certified?
Is the hardware briefly described and placed among comparable open and proprietary equipment in its field?

items.topic: What is new and its advantages
items.question: Does the description focus on the customization, how it differs from existing hardware and what it gains (cost, ease of use, extensibility)?

items.topic: Bullet points on uses for other researchers
items.question: Are three to five bullet points given on how other researchers, in or outside the field, could use the hardware?
Are the design files editable source files, shared in an approved repository, as supplementary material or in the text?

items.topic: Summary table of every design file
items.question: Does a table list every design file with its name, file type, open license and location (URL or with the article)?

items.topic: Short description of each design file
items.question: Is each listed design file described in one or two sentences?

items.topic: Software and firmware included and described
items.question: Are all software and firmware used to build and run the hardware in the repository, described, and commented?
Does the bill list every costed component with quantity, unit and total cost and currency, a source, and a material type?
Do the bill's designators match those of the design files, or is the correspondence explained (a long bill shared as a spreadsheet)?
Could a reader rebuild the hardware from these step-by-step instructions alone?
Are the design decisions explained (and characterized where possible), with the alternatives that were tried?

items.topic: Visuals tied to design files and parts
items.question: Do schematics, images or videos support the steps, which refer to the summarized design files and bill-of-materials parts?
Are potential safety concerns of building the hardware pointed out?
Are step-by-step instructions for operating the hardware safely and correctly given, with visuals where needed?
Are potential hazards of operating the hardware pointed out?

items.topic: Demonstrated on a relevant use case
items.question: Is the hardware shown working on a specific, relevant scientific application?
Is performance characterized across its operating parameters (e.g. accuracy, precision, range), against a reference where possible?
Is there a bulleted list of what the hardware can do and where it falls short?
If the work involved people or animals, is informed consent confirmed, or animal-welfare compliance (ARRIVE and the law, sex reported) stated?
Does a CRediT statement give each author's contribution roles?
Are non-author contributors thanked and every funder and grant number named, or the absence of specific funding stated?
Do the authors declare any financial or personal interests that could bear on the work, or state that there are none?
Are the original hardware this design customizes and the design-file repository cited, besides the context references?
